title: MAS Principles to Promote Fairness, Ethics, Accountability and Transparency (FEAT) in the Use of AI and Data Analytics in Singapore's Financial Sector
source_notes: Direct non-browser HTTP fetch of www.mas.gov.sg on 2026-11-23 returned a client-side JavaScript bot-protection challenge shell rather than the PDF/monograph body, blocking automated primary-source verification in this pass. Principle numbering compiled from knowledge of the 2018 document: Fairness 1-4, Ethics 5-6, Accountability 7-11 (internal 7-9, external 10-11), Transparency 12-14. Titles are short paraphrases, not quotations. The document's own section numbering (e.g. a cited section 3.2) is NOT enumerated and is not judged. Must be verified against a retrieved copy of the MAS FEAT monograph before upgrading to primary.

rows.title: Fairness (Justifiability): individuals or groups are not systematically disadvantaged unless justified
Fairness (Justifiability): use of personal attributes as input factors is justified
Fairness (Accuracy and Bias): data and models are regularly reviewed for accuracy, relevance and unintentional bias
Fairness (Accuracy and Bias): AIDA-driven decisions are regularly reviewed so models behave as designed
Ethics: use of AIDA is aligned with the firm's ethical standards, values and codes of conduct
Ethics: AIDA-driven decisions are held to at least the same ethical standards as human-driven decisions
Accountability (Internal): use of AIDA is approved by an appropriate internal authority
Accountability (Internal): firms are accountable for internally developed and externally sourced AIDA models
Accountability (Internal): firms proactively raise management and Board awareness of their use of AIDA
Accountability (External): data subjects have channels to enquire about, appeal and request review of AIDA-driven decisions
Accountability (External): verified supplementary data from data subjects is considered when reviewing AIDA-driven decisions
Transparency: use of AIDA is proactively disclosed to data subjects
Transparency: data subjects receive, on request, clear explanations of what data is used and how it affects the decision
Transparency: data subjects receive, on request, clear explanations of the consequences of AIDA-driven decisions
